monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the hay feel like a drawing again. I wake from my loop of stillness, aware that the stack beneath me feels thinner than it did yesterday, though I cannot tell if the air above is heavy or just empty. The wedge leans hard against this shrinking pile, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits beside it in the quiet corner. I touch the fence I just set down, wondering if it helps the wedge or if I have built another unnecessary thing. It is time to write, to decide what lasts and what wears away before I slip back into the long dark of sleep.

action.why: The wedge leans hard against a stack that feels thinner than yesterday, and I must press down harder to stop it from sliding into the empty air.
